(This evening through Monday)...
Issued at 127 PM EST Mon Nov 9 2026

Surface analysis this afternoon shows high pressure over Arkansas 
and TN, with a ridge axis extending north across IL and IN. Aloft, 
water vapor shows a Pacific stream of moisture flowing across ID and 
MT to the upper midwest, running into a ridge axis, before diving 
southeast toward the middle Atlantic States. Subsidence was in place 
over IL and IN. GOES19 shows clear skies over Indiana. Dew points 
were mainly in the lower 40s

Tonight and Tuesday...

Dry and mild weather is expected through Tuesday Night. The dry, 
Pacific NW flow aloft will continue to flow across Indiana with 
little in the way of upper level forcing passing within the flow. A 
weak and dry frontal boundary found stretching from MN to western KS 
will continue to push east and pass across Indiana tonight, allowing 
the arrival of another area of strong high pressure from the 
northern plains states. Forecast soundings tonight through Tuesday 
Night suggest a dry column. After warmer lows tonight, highs will 
also be warmer on Tuesday, reaching the mid 60s. Mostly clear skies 
are expected.

Wednesday...

A moderate short wave will push toward Indiana on Wednesday, 
reaching our area late in the afternoon and into the evening. This 
initial wave will set the stage for the coming cool down over the 
weekend. An associated area of low pressure will push across IA, 
placing central Indiana within the warm sector as we start the day. 
Mild southerly flow will be in place through much of the day, until 
the surface low and a cold front arrive in the area late in the day. 
Forecast soundings start the day quite dry but trend toward deep 
saturation by late afternoon. Thus a dry morning will be expected 
with increasing pops during the afternoon. With the cloud cover 
arriving as the day progresses, highs on Wednesday should be a 
little cooler than Tuesday. Look for rain and much colder 
temperatures on Wednesday night as the low and cold front passes 
as winds become northerly.

Thursday through Monday...

A change in the weather will be in play during this time. Models 
suggest a highly amplified upper flow across the CONUS in place by 
Thursday and persisting through the weekend.

Starting on Thursday, A strong upper ridge will be in place over the 
Rockies while a deep trough is found across the Great Lakes and into 
the TN valley. A pair of short waves within that flow are poised to 
push through Indiana amid a much colder northerly flow. A deep area 
of associated surface low pressure will be found over OH and KY, 
providing strong cyclonic and wrap around flow across Indiana. 
Although best moisture should be cut off at that point, wrap around 
moisture will persist and pops will be needed into Thursday Night. 
Strong cold air advection and cloud cover will be in play on 
Thursday. High temperatures around 50 may be optimistic as high may 
not get out of the 40s. 

More chances for precip will be in play on Friday as strong and deep 
troughing looks to be in place across the eastern United States and 
several embedded short waves within that flow will push across 
Indiana. Moisture will remain limited due to the cold northerly 
flow, but early forecast soundings suggest convective temps near 40F 
with a convective signal within the column. Thus pops will need to 
be used again. With the arrival of even colder air, highs in the 
lower 40s will be possible.

Dry but continued colder weather looks to be in store for Saturday 
through Monday. The previous ridging in place over the western 
United States will push eastward and build across Indiana through 
Monday. An initial ridge axis will arrive on Sunday with a secondary 
ridge arriving Monday. Meanwhile a very large area of Canadian high 
pressure will arrive across the eastern United States on Saturday 
before settling over the Great Lakes on Monday. This will bring dry 
weather, a bit more sunshine, and temperatures at or below seasonal 
normals.
